content:
Three dimensional geometry looks heavy, but the basics carry most marks. Master distance, the section formula and octants first. So the smart move is to bank those marks. Try the free JEE 3D Geometry online test below. It gives 15 solved MCQs with instant scoring. Aim for 12.

What JEE asks from 3D geometry

  • Distance between two points in space.
  • Section formula, and the midpoint as its special case.
  • Which octant a point sits in.
  • Where a plane cuts a segment, and in what ratio.
  • Simple loci, like distance from an axis.
  • Foot of a perpendicular dropped onto an axis.

Formulas and facts to revise first

  • Use distance = root of (Δx² + Δy² + Δz²).
  • Split a segment with the section formula ratio m to n.
  • Read octants from the signs of x, y and z.
  • Get distance from the x axis as root of (y² + z²).
  • Find the centroid by averaging the three vertices.

Mistakes that cost JEE marks

  • Swapping internal and external division signs.
  • Using distance from a plane instead of an axis.
  • Misreading an octant when one sign turns negative.
  • Forgetting z in the space distance formula.
  • Reversing a ratio, and so flipping the point.

quiz.title: JEE 3D Geometry Quiz
quiz.intro: Fifteen JEE-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: JEE Maths DPP: Three Dimensional Geometry

questions.q: The perpendicular distance of P(3, 4, 5) from the y-axis is:
questions.explanation: Distance from the y-axis is root of (x² + z²). So it is root of (9 + 25) = √34.

questions.q: In what ratio does the yz-plane divide the segment from (−2, 4, 7) to (3, −5, 8)?
questions.explanation: The yz-plane means x = 0, so the ratio is −x₁/x₂ = 2/3. A positive value marks internal division, so 2:3 internally.

questions.q: Which pair of equations represents the x-axis?
questions.explanation: On the x-axis both y and z stay zero. So y = 0 and z = 0 together define it.
Here AB = AC = √29 and BC = 2√29. Since AB + AC = BC, the three points lie on one line.

questions.q: The point (3, −4, −5) lies in which octant?
questions.explanation: The signs are (+, −, −). That combination belongs to Octant VIII.
The gaps are −4, 2 and 0. So the distance is root of (16 + 4 + 0) = 2√5.

questions.q: A point moves so its distance from the yz-plane is twice its distance from the xz-plane. Its locus is:
questions.explanation: Distance from the yz-plane is |x| and from the xz-plane is |y|. So |x| = 2|y|, which squares to x² = 4y².

questions.q: The locus of a point with y = 0 and z = 0 is:
questions.explanation: With y and z both zero, x stays free. So the locus is the x-axis.

questions.q: The distance of P(−4, 3, 5) from the origin is:
questions.explanation: Distance is root of (16 + 9 + 25) = √50. So it equals 5√2.

questions.q: If the distance between (a, 0, 1) and (0, 1, 2) is √27, then a is:
questions.explanation: The distance formula gives a² + 1 + 1 = 27. So a² = 25 and a = ±5.

questions.q: The octant with coordinate signs (−, +, −) is:
questions.explanation: The pair (−, +) sits in the second quadrant, and a negative z drops below. That gives Octant VI.

questions.q: The midpoint of the segment joining (3, 4, 5) and (1, 2, 3) is:
questions.explanation: Average the coordinates in pairs. So the midpoint is (2, 3, 4).

questions.q: Which point is farthest from the origin?
questions.explanation: The squared distances are 9, 12, 11 and 18. The largest is 18, so (1, 1, 4) wins.

questions.q: The centroid of the triangle with vertices (2, 4, 6), (3, 6, 9) and (1, −1, 0) is:
questions.explanation: Average each coordinate across the three vertices. So the centroid is (2, 3, 5).

questions.q: If x = y = z ≠ 0, the point lies on:
options: a line equally inclined to all axes
questions.explanation: All points with x = y = z lie on a diagonal through the origin. That line is equally inclined to the three axes.
